source.note: A birth by day in Dinamrityu: the Moon in the first pada of Dhanishtha or Hasta, the second of Vishakha or Ardra, the third of Uttara Bhadrapada or Ashlesha, or the fourth of Bharani or Mula; the child dies very soon. Phaladeepika names it without defining it; Sastri's footnote quotes Kalaprakasika for its padas, Ojha's commentary gives the same, and both say it counts only by day, a night birth bearing no fault (C393). Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.

A birth by day in Dinaroga (the verse's ruk): the Moon in the first pada of Ashlesha or Uttara Bhadrapada, the second of Bharani or Mula, the third of Uttara Phalguni or Shravana, or the fourth of Swati or Mrigashira; the child dies very soon. Phaladeepika names it without defining it; Sastri's footnote quotes Kalaprakasika for its padas, Ojha's commentary gives the same, and both say it counts only by day, a night birth bearing no fault (C393). Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.

A birth in the nakshatra's four ghatis of poison (vishaghati); the child dies very soon. The verse gives no table and Sastri none; Ojha's commentary gives each star's, from Ashwini's 50th ghati to its 54th, and counts them as sixtieths of the star's own span, so each window is parts s+1 to s+4 of 60. His table takes the common value in the five stars where Raman's Muhurtha differs (C165), and the muhurta module ships neither (C394). Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.

A birth in a gandanta: the father, the mother or the child dies, and a child that lives becomes a king. The translator sends the word to ch. 1 v. 4, the closing part of Scorpio, Pisces and Cancer, so it is read as the Moon's or the lagna's junction there: BPHS ch. 92's nakshatra and lagna gandantas, named by key, which bound it in ghatikas where Phaladeepika gives no span; the tithi gandanta, no junction of signs, is not named. The verse's first figure, a birth at a sign's junction joined or aspected by malefics, and its third, at any of the four junctions, bound nothing (C381) and are not built. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.

The Moon at her mrityu bhaga in a kendra or the eighth: death. v. 10 gives her degree in each sign, the row MRITYU_BHAGA_MOON_BRIHAT_PRAJAPATYA holds; v. 11's other row is the lagna's (C380), PHALADEEPIKA_LAGNA_AT_A_MRITYU_BHAGA. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.

A birth with the lagna at its mrityu bhaga: the native is short-lived. The verse gives a row of degrees "held by some" and says one born in them has lived his span, naming no body where v. 10 names the Moon; Ojha tabulates it as the lagna's, and Jataka Parijata's translator's lagna row agrees in nine cells (C380), so it reads the lagna in MRITYU_BHAGA_LAGNA_PHALADEEPIKA, in any house. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.

Malefics in the eighth and the kendras: the child dies soon. "The kendras" is read as a malefic in at least one. The verse closes "if no benefic is in a kendra, nor a benefic's conjunction or aspect", which the Sanskrit lays on all seven of its figures and Sastri lists as an eighth (C379). His "no benefic occupies or aspects a kendra" cannot hold, since Jupiter in any house stands in a kendra or aspects one, so it is read as Ojha reads it: no benefic in a kendra, and none joining or aspecting the lagna, the Moon or the figure's malefics. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.

The lagna lord very strong, in a kendra, aspected by benefics and by no malefic, wards off death and gives a long life. The antidotes stand after the evils, so they ship as rules of their own, which every evil of the chapter names; v. 22, a strong Jupiter alone in the lagna, is BPHS ch. 10 v. 3 and is named as ARISHTA_BHANGA_STRONG_JUPITER_IN_LAGNA rather than written twice. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.

The waxing Moon in a trikona, the eleventh or a kendra, in a sign or navamsha of the Sun, the Moon or Jupiter, wards off all ills completely. Waxing is read as the bright half. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.

No malefic in the first, fourth, fifth, seventh, eighth, ninth or tenth, and the lagna lord and Jupiter in kendras: a hundred years free from disease, which the chapter's own index counts among the yogas countering arishta. Read from V. Subrahmanya Sastri's 1937 translation, the Sanskrit checked in Gopesh Kumar Ojha's 1975 commentary.
